boundary.operation: Consume the maximal CSS number prefix at the current parse-that position and return the CSS Syntax §4.3.13 semantic triple.
boundary.maximality: A dot is consumed only with a following ASCII digit; e/E and its optional sign are consumed only with a following ASCII digit. When exponent syntax is complete, the literal e/E is inside the consumed extent.
boundary.value: Base-10 interpretation required by §4.3.13, carried by ECMAScript binary64 Number(consumedRepresentation): precision rounds to binary64, overflow is signed Infinity, and underflow can be signed zero. Public equality is Object.is, preserving negative zero. This explicit carrier boundary grants no arithmetic, math-function, contextual-range, computed-value, or serialization-policy credit.
boundary.type: integer only when neither a fractional part nor exponent is consumed; otherwise number.
boundary.sign: The consumed leading + or -, otherwise null.
boundary.result_object: Reflect.ownKeys must be exactly the three strings value, type, and sign. Object.getPrototypeOf must be Object.prototype. Each key must be an own writable, enumerable, configurable data property; accessors, symbols, non-enumerable surplus, null/custom prototypes, raw/parts/span fields, and any other own keys fail.
boundary.spelling_and_source: The harness observes the exact consumed representation as source.slice(entryOffset, finalOffset) in same-input UTF-16 code units. It earns no raw/preprocessed correspondence or original-source mapping credit; those belong to SYNTAX-SOURCE-MAP.
boundary.failure: If no CSS number starts at the current position, fail without consumption. This internal grammar parser emits no public API diagnostic object.
boundary.composition: The same consuming parser is used by number, integer, percentage, and dimension witnesses. Integer checks the returned type; percentage consumes % afterward; dimension consumes an identifier/unit afterward.
excluded: token, atom, component-value, CST, lexer, scanner, cursor or source-slicing implementation layer
percentage versus dimension dispatch and ident-sequence conformance
unit classification, contextual bounds, math functions, complete-input/EOF diagnostics
numeric evaluation beyond literal base-10 interpretation, canonical serialization and computed values
